goal.source_text: More downforce without going over 15 N of drag at 25 m/s. You can change the angle, span, flap and endplates. Keep the chord.
assumptions: Chord, airfoil, mounts and ride height stay fixed.

payload.explanation: Raising AoA from 6 to 8 deg gave downforce +12.5% and drag +23.8% to 14.9 N, just under the 15 N limit. Three predictions hit; L/D fell 9.08%, slightly beyond the predicted -8%. Induced drag rose 26.7% (CL² effect) versus profile drag 9.51%, and stall margin dropped to 4.17 deg.
payload.lesson: Induced drag grows faster than downforce with angle of attack, so L/D keeps falling and the drag limit caps further AoA gains.

beliefs.text: Induced drag grows faster than downforce with angle of attack, so L/D keeps falling and the drag limit caps further AoA gains.

payload.rationale: Drag is mostly induced (12.7 N of 14.9 N) and sits near the 15 N limit. Taller endplates and more span raise effective aspect ratio, cutting induced drag and freeing headroom for later downforce gains.

payload.explanation: Raising endplate height from 200 to 300 mm lifted effective aspect ratio 15.4%, cutting induced drag 4.80% and total drag 2.91% (just short of the predicted range). Downforce rose 4.83%. Stall margin fell 24.4% (4.17 to 3.15 deg), unpredicted: higher CL pushes the wing closer to stall.
payload.lesson: Endplate height raises effective aspect ratio and CL cheaply, but it erodes stall margin, so check stall before stacking more loading.

payload.explanation: Flap chord rose from 0.3 to 0.35 at 15 deg. All four predictions landed: downforce +2.30%, drag +4.21%, stall margin -3.3%, L/D -1.83%. Drag reached 15.1 N, breaching the 15.0 N limit. Induced drag (+4.66%) rose with CL (+2.31%), since span efficiency was unchanged, and profile drag added +1.95%.
payload.lesson: Flap chord gains downforce only about 2% per step while induced drag grows faster, so with thin drag slack it is infeasible.

payload.explanation: Span rose 850 to 950 mm, lifting effective aspect ratio 7.04% as predicted, but induced drag rose 8.85% instead of falling. Downforce jumped 14.1% (CL +2.11%), so induced drag grew with the lift squared and outweighed the AR gain. Drag hit 15.8 N, breaking the 15.0 N limit, so rejected.
payload.lesson: When span adds area and lift at fixed chord, induced drag rises with lift; longer span does not cut drag under a drag cap.

payload.explanation: Span 850→870 mm raised downforce 2.8% and drag 1.92%, both within the predicted ranges. Effective aspect ratio rose 1.41%, but induced drag still rose 1.82% and profile drag 2.48% from the larger area. Stall margin fell 2.91%, to 3.06 deg. Design stayed feasible, so accepted.
payload.lesson: Extra span gives downforce faster than drag, but wing area adds profile drag and cuts stall margin, so keep steps small.
